# SonarQube CLI

> Code quality and security in your terminal. Scan, integrate, and fix issues — locally or with AI.

- Version: 1.11.0
- Install (Linux/macOS): curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SonarSource/sonarqube-cli/refs/heads/master/user-scripts/install.sh | bash
- Install (Windows): irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SonarSource/sonarqube-cli/refs/heads/master/user-scripts/install.ps1 | iex
- Machine-readable schema: https://sonarsource.com/sonarqube/cli/data/commands.json
- Source: https://github.com/SonarSource/sonarqube-cli
- Commands reference: https://sonarsource.com/sonarqube/cli/commands.html

## Quick Start
sonar auth login
sonar integrate claude

## For AI Agents
Use `sonar list issues --format toon` to output issues in a format optimized for LLM consumption.
Use `sonar list projects` to discover available projects before running analysis.
Commands marked with * require prior authentication via `sonar auth login`.
Aliases are shown next to a command name as `name|alias`.

## Commands

### sonar auth
Manage authentication tokens and credentials

### sonar auth login
Authenticate via browser or an existing token and save credentials in the system keychain. For CI and automation, use environment variables instead: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-cli/using-sonarqube-cli/environment-variables
Usage: sonar auth login [-s <value>] [-o <value>] [--with-token]

Options:
  --server, -s  <string>   SonarQube Server URL, SonarQube Cloud EU (https://sonarcloud.io), or SonarQube Cloud US (https://sonarqube.us). Defaults to SonarQube Cloud EU.
  --org, -o  <string>   SonarQube Cloud organization key (required for SonarQube Cloud)
  --with-token   Read an existing token from standard input

Examples:
  sonar auth login
  sonar auth login -s https://sonarqube.my.com/sonarqube

### sonar auth org *
Switch the active SonarQube Cloud organization without logging in again
Usage: sonar auth org [org]

### sonar auth logout
Remove active connection token from keychain
Usage: sonar auth logout

Examples:
  sonar auth logout

### sonar auth status
Show active authentication connection with token verification
Usage: sonar auth status [--format <value>]

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format

Examples:
  sonar auth status

### sonar list
List issues, projects and organizations from SonarQube Cloud or Server

### sonar list issues *
Search for issues in SonarQube
Usage: sonar list issues [-p <value>] [--statuses <value>] [--severities <value>] [--format <value>] [--branch <value>] [--pull-request <value>] [--file <value>] [--new-code] [--page-size <value>] [--page <value>]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key
  --statuses  <string>   Filter by status (comma-separated list of: OPEN, CONFIRMED, FALSE_POSITIVE, ACCEPTED, FIXED). Defaults to OPEN, CONFIRMED.
  --severities  <string>   Filter by severity. Valid values depend on server mode — Multi-Quality Rule (MQR) mode: INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, BLOCKER; Standard Experience mode: INFO, MINOR, MAJOR, CRITICAL, BLOCKER.
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --branch  <string>   Branch name. Cannot be combined with --pull-request.
  --pull-request  <string>   Pull request ID. Cannot be combined with --branch.
  --file  <string>   Limit results to one file, or to a directory's own files (not its subdirectories): a full path from the project root, or just a name if it matches only one
  --new-code   Only show issues on new code (the leak period)
  --page-size  <number>   Page size (1-500)
  --page  <number>   Page number

Examples:
  sonar list issues -p my-project
  sonar list issues -p my-project --format toon

### sonar list projects *
Search for projects in SonarQube
Usage: sonar list projects [-q <value>] [--format <value>] [--page <value>] [--page-size <value>]

Options:
  --query, -q  <string>   Search query to filter projects by name or key
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --page  <number>   Page number
  --page-size  <number>   Page size (1-500)

Examples:
  sonar list projects
  sonar list projects -q my-project
  sonar list projects --page 2 --page-size 50

### sonar list orgs|org *
List organizations you have access to (SonarQube Cloud only)
Usage: sonar list orgs [--format <value>] [--page <value>] [--page-size <value>]

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --page  <number>   Page number
  --page-size  <number>   Page size (1-500)

### sonar quality-gate|qg
Fetch quality gate status from SonarQube Cloud or Server

### sonar quality-gate status *
Show the quality gate verdict for a project
Usage: sonar quality-gate status [-p <value>] [--format <value>] [--branch <value>] [--pull-request <value>] [--all] [--category <value>] [--top <value>] [file]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --branch  <string>   Branch name. Cannot be combined with --pull-request.
  --pull-request  <string>   Pull request ID. Cannot be combined with --branch.
  --all   Also show passing conditions. By default only failing conditions are shown.
  --category  <string>   Only show the breakdown for one category of failing conditions
  --top  <number>   Number of entries to include in the breakdown, per condition

### sonar import *
Import repositories from a connected GitHub or Azure DevOps organization into SonarQube (SonarQube Cloud only) [BETA]
Usage: sonar import [--repo <value>] [--all] [--regex <value>] [--non-interactive]

Options:
  --repo  <object>   DevOps platform repository slug (e.g. my-org/my-repo). Repeatable and/or comma-separated to import multiple repositories. Cannot be combined with --all or --regex.
  --all   Import every eligible repository in the organization (not already imported, and allowed by its project visibility settings). Cannot be combined with --repo or --regex.
  --regex  <string>   Import only eligible repositories whose DevOps platform name (not slug) matches this regular expression.

                   Case-sensitive by default; wrap as /pattern/flags to add flags like case-insensitive matching. Cannot be combined with --repo or --all.
                   Examples:
                       --regex "^test-"
                       --regex "/^archived-/i"

  --non-interactive   Skip all prompts; require explicit flags

### sonar api *
Make authenticated API requests to SonarQube
Usage: sonar api [-d <value>] [--verbose] <method> <endpoint>

Options:
  --data, -d  <string>   JSON string for request body. The tool will automatically format as either form data or JSON body.
  --verbose, -v   Print request and response details for debugging.

Examples:
  sonar api get "/api/favorites/search"
  sonar api get "/api/rules/search?organization=my-org&languages=ts"
  sonar api post "/api/user_tokens/generate" --data '{"name":"my-token"}'
  sonar api post "/api/issues/do_transition" --data '{"issue":"AYx1z2","transition":"accept"}'
  sonar api get "/analysis/engine"
  sonar api get "/api/system/status" --verbose
  sonar api post "/api/user_tokens/revoke" --data '{"name":"my-token"}'

### sonar integrate *
Setup SonarQube integration for AI coding agents, git and others

Examples:
  sonar integrate
  sonar integrate claude
  sonar integrate claude --non-interactive

### sonar integrate git *
Install a Git pre-commit hook that scans staged files for secrets and dependency risks before each commit, or a Git pre-push hook that scans committed files for secrets before each push.
Usage: sonar integrate git [--hook <value>] [--force] [--non-interactive] [--local] [--global]

Options:
  --hook  <string>   Hook to install: pre-commit (scan staged files) or pre-push (scan files in unpushed commits)
  --force   Overwrite existing hook if it is not from sonar integrate git
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --local   Install the hook for this repository only, instead of globally (workaround for setups where a global hook does not fit, e.g. Husky)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; the hook is installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate git' instead.

Examples:
  sonar integrate git
  sonar integrate git --hook pre-push
  sonar integrate git --global
  sonar integrate git --hook pre-push --global --non-interactive

### sonar integrate claude *
Setup SonarQube integration for Claude Code. This will install secrets scanning hooks, configure Vortex analysis and MCP Server.
Usage: sonar integrate claude [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate claude' instead.

### sonar integrate copilot *
Setup SonarQube integration for GitHub Copilot CLI. This will install secrets scanning hooks, configure Vortex analysis and MCP Server.
Usage: sonar integrate copilot [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate copilot' instead.

### sonar integrate codex *
Setup SonarQube integration for Codex. Installs a UserPromptSubmit hook for prompt secrets scanning, secrets-on-read instructions, and the MCP server. When Vortex is available, also installs startup context hooks, analysis hooks, and end-of-turn analysis instructions.
Usage: sonar integrate codex [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate codex' instead.

### sonar integrate antigravity *
Setup SonarQube integration for Antigravity. Installs secrets scanning hooks, prompt-secrets instructions, and Vortex Context.
Usage: sonar integrate antigravity [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate antigravity' instead.

### sonar integrate cursor *
Setup SonarQube integration for Cursor. This will configure the SonarQube MCP Server, install secrets scanning hooks, and configure Vortex analysis. Note: Cursor's cloud/background agents only pick up project-level hooks, not global ones.
Usage: sonar integrate cursor [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate cursor' instead.

### sonar integrate opencode *
Setup SonarQube integration for OpenCode. This will install secrets scanning hooks, configure Vortex analysis and MCP Server.
Usage: sonar integrate opencode [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate opencode' instead.

### sonar integrate devin *
Setup SonarQube integration for Devin. This will install secrets scanning hooks, configure Vortex analysis and MCP Server.
Usage: sonar integrate devin [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate devin' instead.

### sonar integrate pi *
Setup SonarQube integration for Pi. This will install secrets scanning hooks, configure Vortex analysis and the SonarQube MCP Server.
Usage: sonar integrate pi [--non-interactive] [--global]

Options:
  --non-interactive   Non-interactive mode (no prompts)
  --global, -g   Backwards compatibility; integrations are installed globally by default [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9.0 and will be removed in a future version. Use 'sonar integrate pi' instead.

### sonar context
Augment AI agents with context from your codebase
Usage: sonar context [action] [args]

### sonar analyze *
Analyze code for quality and security issues

### sonar analyze secrets *
Scan files or stdin for hardcoded secrets
Usage: sonar analyze secrets [--stdin] [paths]

Options:
  --stdin   Read from standard input instead of paths

Examples:
  sonar analyze secrets src/config.ts
  sonar analyze secrets src/file1.ts src/file2.ts
  cat .env | sonar analyze secrets --stdin

### sonar analyze dependency-risks *
Analyze project dependencies for security and license risks
Usage: sonar analyze dependency-risks [-p <value>] [--format <value>] [--statuses <value>] [--min-severity <value>]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key (auto-detected when omitted)
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --statuses  <string>   Filter issues by status

  Raw:       new | open | confirm | accept | safe | fixed
  Presets:   active | to_fix | all
    active:  new, open, confirm
    to_fix:  new, open, confirm, accept
    all:     new, open, confirm, accept, safe, fixed

Presets and raw statuses can be combined; the resulting set is the union.

Examples:
    --statuses active
    --statuses new,confirm
    --statuses active,safe

  --min-severity  <string>   Minimum severity level to include. Allowed values: BLOCKER, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO (default: all severities)

### sonar analyze agentic *
Run server-side Vortex analysis. Limitations apply
Usage: sonar analyze agentic [--file <value>] [--staged] [--base <value>] [-p <value>] [--force] [--depth <value>] [--format <value>] [--branch <value>]

Options:
  --file  <string>   Analyze specific file(s) instead of the git change set (repeatable)
  --staged   Analyze staged files only (git diff --cached)
  --base  <string>   Analyze files changed vs a branch or ref (e.g. main)
  --project, -p  <string>   SonarQube project key (overrides auto-detected project)
  --force   Skip the large change set confirmation prompt
  --depth  <string>   Analysis depth: STANDARD (fast) or DEEP (cross-file). Default: STANDARD for one --file; DEEP otherwise.
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --branch  <string>   Branch name for analysis context

### sonar remediate *
Trigger AI agent remediation for eligible issues (SonarQube Cloud only)
Usage: sonar remediate [-p <value>] [--issues <value>]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   SonarQube Cloud project key (overrides auto-detected project)
  --issues  <string>   Comma-separated issue keys to remediate non-interactively (max 20). Required when stdin is not a TTY.

### sonar link *
Link a project to the active connection in .sonar-config.json

### sonar link list *
List linked projects at, under or enclosing a path as JSON, nearest first
Usage: sonar link list [--path <value>] [--pattern <value>] [--page <value>] [--page-size <value>]

Options:
  --path  <string>   File or directory to list projects for (default: current directory)
  --pattern  <string>   Only list projects whose key or directory matches this regex
  --page  <number>   Page number
  --page-size  <number>   Page size (1-100)

### sonar config
Configure CLI settings

### sonar config get
Print a stored sonar config value
Usage: sonar config get [--format <value>] <key>

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format

### sonar config list
Print every sonar config key with its current value
Usage: sonar config list [--format <value>] [--only-set]

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --only-set   Only show keys that currently have a value

### sonar config set
Store a sonar config value
Usage: sonar config set <key> [value]

### sonar config unset
Remove a stored sonar config value
Usage: sonar config unset <key>

### sonar architecture|arch
Read and set the architecture of a project

### sonar architecture current
Read the current architecture

### sonar architecture current get *
Current architecture, at most 150 nodes, 20 dependencies and 5 feedback pairs across languages; drill down with --component and --depth
Usage: sonar architecture current get [-p <value>] [--component <value>] [--depth <value>] [--language <value>] [--format <value>]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key
  --component  <string>   Node key to start below, from a previous current get
  --depth  <string>   Levels below the start node (default 1)
  --language  <string>   Only this language (default: all)
  --format  <string>   Output format (default: text on a terminal, toon otherwise)

### sonar architecture intended
Read and set the intended architecture

### sonar architecture intended get *
Intended architecture; full JSON can be saved with intended set, --component/--depth give partial views, --language exports are CLI-only and cannot be passed to MCP architecture_set
Usage: sonar architecture intended get [-p <value>] [--component <value>] [--depth <value>] [--language <value>] [--format <value>]

Options:
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key
  --component  <string>   Group key to start below, e.g. Domain/Billing
  --depth  <string>   Levels of groups below the start group (default: all)
  --language  <string>   Only this language (default: all)
  --format  <string>   Output format (default: text on a terminal, toon otherwise)

### sonar architecture intended set *
Replace the intended architecture with a file shaped like the output of intended get --format json
Usage: sonar architecture intended set [--file <value>] [--dry-run] [-p <value>]

Options:
  --file  <string>   Intended architecture JSON file
  --dry-run   Validate and show the changes, removals first, without writing
  --project, -p  <string>   Project key

### sonar architecture install-skill *
Install the architecture skill for Claude Code and Cursor in this repository [BETA]
Usage: sonar architecture install-skill [--global] [--force]

Options:
  --global   Install in the home directory instead of the repository
  --force   Replace a SKILL.md that was not written by this command

### sonar system
System diagnostics and maintenance commands for the SonarQube CLI installation

### sonar system status
Show overall system status: authentication, installed binaries, and integrations
Usage: sonar system status [--format <value>] [--json]

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format
  --json   Output as JSON for machine consumption [DEPRECATED] This option is deprecated since 1.9 and will be removed in a future version. Use '--format json' instead.

### sonar system reset
Reset the CLI to factory defaults: remove tokens, binaries, integrations, cached files, and local stats data. Pass --all to also remove CLI configuration (sonar config).
Usage: sonar system reset [--force] [--all]

Options:
  --force   Skip the interactive confirmation prompt (required for non-interactive use)
  --all   Also remove CLI configuration (sonar config), including network and telemetry configuration

### sonar allowlist
Manage local allowlists for SonarQube analyzers

### sonar allowlist secrets
Manage the local sonar-secrets allowlist for known-safe values (test fixtures, sample tokens)

### sonar allowlist secrets show
List entries in the sonar-secrets allowlist
Usage: sonar allowlist secrets show

### sonar allowlist secrets add
Add a secret value to the sonar-secrets allowlist (interactive; requires a real terminal, not usable by agents or scripts)
Usage: sonar allowlist secrets add

### sonar allowlist secrets remove
Remove an entry from the sonar-secrets allowlist by key
Usage: sonar allowlist secrets remove <key>

### sonar allowlist secrets clear
Remove all entries from the sonar-secrets allowlist
Usage: sonar allowlist secrets clear [--force]

Options:
  --force   Skip the interactive confirmation prompt (required for non-interactive use)

### sonar update
Update SonarQube CLI to the latest version

### sonar update status
Check for a newer version without installing
Usage: sonar update status [--format <value>]

Options:
  --format  <string>   Output format
